paper_metadata.title: Microstructure Tailoring of Novel Titanium Alloys

evidence.quote: many titanium alloys with bimodal structure have been fabricated by rapid solidification and powder metallurgy and have exhibited a combination of high strength and large plasticity .
A nanostructure-dendrite bimodal microstructure was obtained by modification of the Ti50Cu23Ni20Sn7 bulk metallic glass alloy via the addition of Ta or Nb;
It has been reported that cryogenic rolling and low-temperature annealing was used to fabricate a multimodal grain structure and a fine-grained matrix surrounding coarse grains in commercial Ti.
This multi-model structured Ti exhibited yield strength of up to 926 MPa and a large fracture elongation of 23%.

a similar multimodal structure was developed in biomedical β-type Ti–24Nb–4Zr–7.9Sn alloy, which exhibited an ultimate tensile strength of 850 MPa, a high recoverable strain of 3.3%, and Young’s modulus of 42 GPa.

evidence.quote: A nanostructure-dendrite bimodal microstructure was obtained by modification of the Ti50Cu23Ni20Sn7 bulk metallic glass alloy via the addition of Ta or Nb; the resulting material exhibited an ultimate compressive strength of up to 2.4 GPa and a plastic strain of 14.5%.

the bimodal microstructure in Ti60Cu16.8-Ni14.4Nb80Sn4.8 alloy had 20 vol% dendritic bcc β-Ti and a 50 nm matrix with mixed phases of hcp α-Ti, Ti2Cu, and Ti2Ni intermetallic compounds; this material exhibited yield strength of 1313 MPa and a plastic strain of 8.9%.
